A PERFECT WORLD

The whole world's a fight I can't get no peace
My mind gets disrupted when it's at ease

I'm surprised you've forgotten so soon
There's so much more than what you've been told
Rise up in rebellion, could you be so bold?

A world lacking communion, only me's and I's
Through competition our brotherhood has been broken
As no one's acknowledged these words that I've spoken

Number one built the Titanic yet down it sank
There's still time left to return these ideas you've been sold
Rise up in rebellion, could you be so bold?

Those same people send other mother's sons to war
I could be like you or maybe someone else
One step towards them and one away from myself
Sometimes they see me and ask me "How I feel?"

If you feel trapped like a rat in this world so cold
Rise up in rebellion, could you be so bold?

I'll keep on fighting no matter what's in store
But at least I'll know what I'm fighting for
My own little peace and quiet in this world so vast
This world makes me dizzy because it's moving to fast

Stop going for broke when you'll win if you hold
Rise up in rebellion, could you be so bold?

They get so stressed out playing all their Wall Street games

AROUND THE KING'S TABLE

All raise glasses to propose a toast
Tilt back brims to honor a host

cards.summary: A printed document on a white sheet of paper.
cards.typed_words:
Poem 1
Hidden Evils

A crying teen wonders how much more she can handle
While mangy dogs dig through trash and howl at the wind
The priest in the church lights a holy candle
For all of his lost children who have sinned

Son lays awake all night dreaming of tomorrow
Grandmother prays for her soul to be saved
Father works his second job, eyes full of sorrow
Single mother wonders how the bills will get paid

A child born of racists, his heart fills with hate
Paint chips off the walls of the liquor store
An abandoned building becomes home to a family of eight
The donation bin stays empty while collecting for the poor

A pigeon wanders aimlessly unsure of where to look for food
A wrinkled and ripped newspaper blows around in the park
A homeless man sleeping on a bench awakes in a foul mood
As night falls all that's wrong with the world is covered by dark

This poem was an attempt to break my rhyming pattern of consecutive twos. I
am also a fan of this rhyming scheme because it is a little harder for me because
I'm not used to it. I tried to show all the evils in the world that we, as a society,
have a tendency to overlook because they're commonplace. I started by only
rhyming in the 2nd and 4th verses but didn't like the end result so I redid the other
two lines so that they rhymed.

cards.typed_words:
Tom Jensen
Ten of my better poems created in this class
December 5, 1999

Poem 1
This is a first draft. It is about my own piece of sanity. A future revision may include lengthening the piece. This poem was inspired by a Pete Townsend tune of the same harmony. I was feeling very stressed and I needed a way to put things in perspective. This did the trick.

SYMPHONY IN MY HEAD
There is a symphony playing in my mind
And it only plays for me
Sometimes I try to write it down
Though it somehow remains free
So pure and true
No pen or paper could ever hold
The only thing that's mine
That I hold in this world so cold
Sometimes the music sounds
When life has got me down
It's the only thing that awakes me from my sorrow
Sometimes the music plays
When my happiness goes away
Reminds me there's always hope for tomorrow

Poem 2
This poem was inspired after I was playing around with some catch phrases. I came up with the catch phrase and wrote the rest of the poem around the concept of "You can call it fate." The rest will be here someday, I hope. This poem ponders over the question of why bad things happen. I think it would be better served with 2 more lines in each stanza.
This is the second draft and a future draft would include the last stanza concluding with the defendant commiting a bad crime.

CALL IT FATE
Birds circle around your home
One more time won't they leave you alone
They flap their wings from side to side
From Mother Nature no man can hide
Being punished for crimes - well, that may be
Crimes against humanity
Just when you though there was no one to see
Now look at your life and who's to blame?
You can call it fate
What a shame?

As your family boasts "You're in the prime of your life"
You go under the doctor's knife
For cancer has no name or face
Unfortunately for you [...cut for the check]
